item.title: Misery Index: Matt Rhule is running out of answers as another Nebraska season spirals out of control
item.description: The Nebraska job is getting to Matt Rhule. A week ago, he started his press conference with a 20-minute soliloquy/opening statement that felt like a therapy session. He spends ridiculous amounts of time arguing with the referees. Now, after firing Dana Holgorsen on Saturday , he’ll soon be on his third offensive coordinator in four seasons. But it’s hard to tell who’s going off the deep end quicker in this relationship — the head coach or a fan base that is finding new ways to be aghast at their program, which has gone from 5-0 to 5-4 and failed to crack 20 points in any of those losses. The latest indignity, the one that demanded Rhule sacrifice a staff member, was a 24-13 loss to Illinois . But in firing Holgorsen, Rhule tacitly admitted how screwed up his whole process has been from the time he’s gotten to Lincoln. Holgorsen, who came from the Mike Leach offensive tree at Texas Tech, was never going to be a great fit in the Big Ten. Rhule hired him anyway. He was also going to be a square peg in a round hole building an offense around Dylan Raiola, a quarterback with limited mobility. Rhule hired him anyway. Then when Raiola transferred to Oregon, they rebuilt it around Anthony Colandrea, who has a lot of running ability. A little more than a week ago, Nebraska announced that Colandrea had signed to return to Nebraska for a fifth year in 2027. Then they turned around and fired Holgorsen, ostensibly meaning Rhule’s next offensive coordinator hire will once again have to fit around a quarterback rather than the other way around. That is, if Rhule stays in Lincoln. Though Nebraska fans have dealt with many losing streaks over the last couple decades, this one is hitting them differently. (In retrospect, the Bo Pelini era looks pretty good, eh?) And what makes it different is Rhule’s contract. After Penn State fired James Franklin a year ago, Nebraska chose to extend Rhule through 2032, saddling the school with a buyout in the $60 million range. Because of Rhule’s close relationship with Penn State athletic director Pat Kraft (they worked together at Temple) and ties to the school (Rhule went to high school in State College and played at Penn State), he was going to be their No. 1 choice. Nebraska felt at the time the program was on the right track and didn’t want to go into coach search mode so they made the long-term investment to keep him. It now looks like the wrong decision, but that’s in the past. The question is what Nebraska can do to now to either triage the situation or extricate the school from it. Fans are mad at everyone, and they’re going to be very loud about it the rest of this season. They could potentially even end the school’s famous sellout streak going back to 1962, which has long been a point of pride for the Cornhuskers. Matt Rhule is 24-23 as head coach of the Nebraska Cornhuskers. item.title: Mourinho talks record win-rate, fixture congestion and international break after Valencia 0-3 Real Madrid
item.description: Mourinho talks record win-rate, fixture congestion and international break after Valencia 0-3 Real Madrid Real Madrid will sign off for the second international break of the season in an emphatic fashion, having secured a comprehensive 3-0 win over Valencia. It was a dominant performance from Los Blancos , who continue their solid run of form since the end of the first international break of the season. Speaking to the media after the game, Jose Mourinho offered his thoughts on a historic personal milestone while throwing a tantrum on the fixture, among other things. A record-breaking win rate Mourinho was informed during the presser that he had just become the coach with the best win percentage in La Liga history, with 97 victories from 126 matches across his two spells at the Bernabeu. “It tells me we have to win the next one. Because… in this life, the beautiful numbers, the ones that have some meaning… people forget. And we don’t feed on numbers from the past; we feed on the present. And we have to win the next one ,” he said. It was a dominant, team-effort for Real Madrid. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) “But I had no idea. And obviously it’s a pride, because the Spanish League has had so many top coaches throughout history. And to be there, with those numbers, is a pride. But, as I say, the next game is the most important thing ,” he added. Mourinho went on to heap praise on his team, particularly for the defensive solidity they have shown and how the team has evolved across the course of this season. “It’s them. It’s them. The credit is for the players. I can’t identify anything in my work that’s the key to… to do it. I do my normal job and they are responding individually and as a team… they are responding in a spectacular way.” “There is a great evolution, but I think that also the fact that today we have had so much possession and… little defensive work, helps. But it must also be said that at the time of losing the ball, we have always had a great reaction ,” he said. Mourinho also dissected why Real Madrid have been so strong defensively, putting out one instance of teamwork. “But in relation to what you say, there is an image in front of my bench, in the second half, where we have lost the ball, Arda is out of position and Kylian makes… a sprint to get to and to close the block on the right side. item.title: JJ Gabriel is taking a huge risk by swapping Man Utd for the developmental graveyard at Real Madrid
item.description: JJ Gabriel Real Madrid risk GFX - GOAL The gifted teenager is facing the toughest possible path to senior football after opting to start a new life in the Spanish capital JJ Gabriel has been the most wanted man in Europe since informing Manchester United of his desire to leave the club in September. Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich have all been chasing the Enfield-born prodigy, while United officials have toiled in vain to convince him to change his mind. At one stage, it looked like Barcelona would win the race, as Gabriel spent weeks training in the city with a personal trainer, but it now appears that they've been pipped to the post by their arch-rivals. Real Madrid have reportedly reached a verbal agreement to sign the 16-year-old on a long-term contract, subject to FIFA regulations on the transfer of minors. Gabriel is registered with United's academy until the end of the 2026-27 campaign, but Real intend to complete the deal in January, with the teenager possessing a European passport through both parents that allows him to exploit a Brexit loophole and join an overseas club in the next transfer window. There are none bigger than Los Blancos, and Gabriel's decision to swap his comfort zone at Old Trafford for the bright lights at the Santiago Bernabeu speaks to his self-confidence. According to Sky Sports , Real emerged as Gabriel's first choice because he and his camp see a clear pathway to the first team. However, a quick look at the club's history with young players suggests that is naïve. He will also face more competition for minutes in the Spanish capital than he would have at any other of his suitors, and indeed United. For all the prestige that comes with wearing that famous white shirt, there is immense pressure to deal with, too. Gabriel will not be trying to follow in the footsteps of a long list of successful academy graduates, but rather buck the trend at a club that has become something of a developmental graveyard. Rare exceptions Of the many youngsters who have been brought to Real over the years, only a select few have become household names at the Bernabeu It is much quicker to run through Real's youth player wins than losses, certainly in recent times. The gold standard is Casemiro, who was the foundational experiment subject for Madrid's plan to pivot from their traditional grassroots ladder to signing U18 or U20 prospects and embedding them immediately in the Castilla ranks to adapt to European football. The Brazil international played 15 matches for the Madrid 'B' team after joining the club from Sao Paulo in 2013, and went on to anchor five Champions League triumphs, before bringing in a €70m plus fee from Man Utd. Fede Valverde, meanwhile, signed from Penarol for just €5m three years after Casemiro. He also became a world-class midfielder in a glorious era for Madrid, and now serves as club captain. item.title: The greatest team to never to win the Champions League? Paolo Maldini, Hernan Crespo, Kaka and AC Milan's super side of 2005
item.description: AC Milan GFX - GOAL Carlo Ancelotti's Rossoneri may have ultimately gained revenge over Liverpool for 'The Miracle of Istanbul', but the team beaten in Turkey was even stronger than the side that triumphed in Athens in 2007 Paolo Maldini remembers very little of the 2007 Champions League final - because he had taken so many painkillers just to get through it . The legendary defender was 38 at the time and in dire need of knee surgery, but there was just no way he was going to sit out AC Milan's meeting with Liverpool in Athens. Just two years previously, the Rossoneri had been the victims of 'The Miracle of Istanbul', where the Reds prevailed on penalties after sensationally coming from three goals down at half-time. Consequently, revenge was all that mattered to Maldini. "We had everything to lose," he told GOAL , "because if we lost again to Liverpool then it would be something very difficult to erase." Milan were, thus, willing to do whatever was required to get over the line in Greece, and both coach Carlo Ancelotti and midfielder Clarence Seedorf admitted afterwards that the Rossoneri hadn't played particularly well in their 2-1 triumph at the Olympic Stadium. They didn't care, though. As Gennaro Gattuso said , "It's our turn to celebrate now." However, even in that moment of release, relief and redemption, the Italy international admitted that the pain of losing the 2005 final would stay with him "for a lifetime" - and that's partly because neither he nor his team-mates will ever be allowed to forget it. Why? Because unlike in 2007, the gulf in quality between the two teams was enormous. Kaka has called the 2007 winners "a beautiful side" , but it was nowhere as good as the one beaten in Istanbul. As ex-Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher admitted on The Overlap , "When you actually look at that team - that team photo before the final - you're thinking that's one of the best teams not just of that era, but one of the best teams ever." So, how on earth did they fail to win a single major trophy that season?... Team of legends Milan added Jaap Stam and Hernan Crespo to a team that romped to the 2003-04 Serie A title Milan should have been bidding for a third consecutive Champions League crown in Istanbul. item.title: ‘No bailout from the ACC’ – Fans split on controversial Miami Hurricanes incomplete pass call
item.description: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images The Miami Hurricanes’ late-game touchdown was ruled an incomplete pass in a decision that many fans are divided on. With a little over three minutes to go in the game, the Hurricanes were on their fourth down at Notre Dame’s 18-yard line. QB Darian Mensah threw a long pass to TE Elija Lofton, who caught it in the air and landed with both feet in the end zone just before Notre Dame S Luke Talich knocked the ball out of his hands just before he went out of bounds. Miami Hurricanes’ incomplete pass has left College Football fans divided A fan on social media shared slow-motion footage of Lofton’s catch from a sideline camera, and it shows the TE landing with both feet just as Talich knocked the ball out of his hands. Rather than providing clarity, the clip has only added to the conversation surrounding the nature of the incomplete pass call from the refs. Understandably, fans couldn’t form any kind of consensus on the matter, with some believing the Hurricanes were unfairly punished, while others justified the call. One fan wrote: “Miami got s****** by the refs. That’s a touchdown.” A second fan agreed, explaining: “The rules get rewritten every day. Complete the reception… Well, now a defensive player can rip the ball out when the player is out of bounds to not allow the receiver to complete the catch.” A third fan suggested the Hurricanes’ luck ran out with this call from the referees: “I know Miami has gotten lucky with questionable calls all season, but I still feel bad that they got screwed by this one.” However, a fourth fan with ties to the Hurricanes defended the call: “I’m a Miami fan; sadly not a catch. Crazy he didn’t secure it, though. Good effort and comeback from UM, great game.” A fifth fan echoed this sentiment: “Did you catch the ball if somebody knocked it out of your hands?” And lastly, a sixth fan seemingly enjoyed this reversal of fortunes in referee decisions for Miami: “No bailout from the ACC on this one. Unlucky.” This has to be one of the most contentious calls of the College Football season, as fans across the country are divided about what the decision should have been. This loss to Notre Dame will cost the Hurricanes their #1 ranking, which will only add to the abject disappointment of losing to a historic rival on such a contentious play. item.title: 'The worst conditions in my 35-year career' - commentating in the FA Cup fog
item.description: One of the most important attributes for a commentator is to be able to see the action you are trying to describe but that became a luxury for BBC Sport's Steve Bower when Altrincham hosted Notts County in an FA Cup tie on Saturday. As thick fog enveloped the Moss Lane ground, he could barely see what was going on in a first-round game being televised live on BBC Two. "One of the more challenging of my long career, that's about 35 years now," said Bower about the experience. "I was reminded by a colleague - maybe I'm a jinx - that we had a similar thing on the BBC about three years ago when we did York against Wigan in the first round and the fog came in. "Tonight was worse. From where we were, opposite the dugouts, once the play went to the centre circle and beyond, we couldn't see a thing. "We couldn't see which team had the ball, let alone which player had the ball after about the 60th minute. Bearing in mind it went to extra-time, it was challenging. "I just kept looking down at my phone and it was text message after text message from people saying, 'You're sounding great, but I can't see a thing'. In the end, you have to roll with it and do the best you can." Notts County progress in FA Cup tie no-one could see 'It's like a spot-the-ball competition' National League Altrincham were on for an upset when they took a 2-1 lead against the League One side but a late Callum Roberts equaliser for County took the game to extra-time before the visiting side won on penalties. "The frustrating thing is that for an hour it was a really good FA Cup tie, it had everything," said Bower. "It was on for another giant-killing script but then the frustrating thing is that it becomes a non-event because, without stating the obvious, people can't see half of it. "Also, it's not then about the tactics, or the shape of it, or the aggression, or the effort because you just can't see it. As a spectacle in trying to describe a game like you normally would, it's impossible." Bower's radio colleagues were not faring much better as they tried to work out what was going on. "I can just about see the bright white numbers on their shirts, but I am struggling to see what is happening on the far side of the pitch," said BBC Radio Nottingham commentator Adam Hassell. Former Notts County striker Mark Stallard, who was also speaking on BBC Radio Nottingham, said: "We're looking around, and here in the press box no-one knows where the ball is! It's like a spot-the-ball competition. "I played in the Notts County cup side against Wimbledon when it was abandoned - they equalised in the second half and I didn't see any of it!" Stallard later said: "We genuinely cannot see the linesman or the players on the far side. It's slightly farcical having to commentate for radio listeners." item.title: There is one thing Manchester City desperately need before their creative players can take over
item.description: There is one thing Manchester City desperately need before their creative players can take over Manchester City were comprehensively beaten by Nottingham Forest 3-1 at The City Ground yesterday. Enzo Maresca’s side were brushed aside both physically and in general play in the opening half-hour by Oliver Glasner’s side. City did fight back in the second half but by then, they had left themselves too much work to do. When Liam Delap scored in the 73rd minute, City were condemned to their third successive defeat in the Premier League. Looking at the City team sheet, they are blessed with a plethora of attacking talent. However, Enzo Maresca’s side lacks the security to properly profit from their abundance of creative and attacking riches. Also, the lack of midfield security is undermining almost every aspect of City’s play. Enzo Maresca has to find balance with his Manchester City lineup, especially in midfield. It isn’t a stretch to say that the starting lineup that Enzo Maresca selected against Nottingham Forest was far too unbalanced. As we have seen throughout this season, a midfield trio of Rayan Cherki, Enzo Fernandez and Elliot Anderson can be too easily bypassed. When you factor in two attacking inverting full-backs which was on display yesterday, a huge flaw in this Manchester City side is exposed. Oliver Glasner set up his team to get at this weakness at The City Ground. His team duly obliged and City came out of yesterday’s match with a litany of concerns. An obvious solution is for Enzo Maresca to find a proper midfield balance. The solution does seem simple. Despite Enzo Maresca’s insistence that Elliot Anderson is a number six, he does his best work alongside a proper number six, playing as an eight. That way he can cover the pitch and play to his strengths rather than be loose with his positioning. That isn’t a knock on Anderson at all. He has been superb for Manchester City this season. However, you do feel that he is being asked to do far too much in a new role for him. The City midfield solution seems to be obvious. Surely, it is time for Enzo Maresca to build his midfield around Ayyoub Bouaddi as the number six with Elliot Anderson in his preferred midfield role. Then one of Rayan Cherki, Enzo Fernandez and Phil Foden can play as the attacking midfielder. Manchester City need security to underpin their play. With a strong midfield base, it should provide exactly what this City side needs. Also, with a sturdy midfield installed, it should also allow Manchester City’s array of attacking talent to be unleashed properly. For me, that seems to be the simple solution to try and give this City side exactly what they sorely lack. The international break does give Enzo Maresca time to have a good look at what has gone wrong for his team. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty Images As the top high school player in Wyoming, Luke Talich received scholarship offers from a few Football Bowl Subdivision programs, including Utah and Washington State. Instead, Talich chose to enroll at Notre Dame as a preferred walk-on in 2023. A year later, he earned a scholarship. Now, Talich will be remembered for years to come. On Saturday night, Talich, a senior safety, made two crucial defensive plays, helping the No. 11 Fighting Irish defeat No. 1 Miami, 31-24, to keep their hopes of advancing to the College Football Playoff alive. Late in the third quarter, Talich picked off Miami quarterback Darian Mensah’s pass near midfield, only Mensah’s second interception this season. The Irish then scored to go ahead 31-17 early in the fourth quarter. After Miami cut its deficit to seven points and had the ball with a chance to tie the game, Talich broke up a pass in the end zone on fourth down with 3:36 remaining, keeping the Irish’s lead intact. Although Miami had one final drive with 57 seconds remaining, Notre Dame’s defense again stopped the Hurricanes (8-1) and gave the Irish (8-1) their biggest regular season victory in decades. It was Notre Dame’s 10th win over the No. 1 team in the Associated Press poll and first since November 2020 when the Irish defeated Clemson, 47-40, in double overtime in a game that only 11,000 people attended due to Covid-19 restrictions. Still, Saturday’s victory at a sold-out Notre Dame Stadium was even more important, as the Irish could have been eliminated from CFP contention if they lost. Notre Dame is No. 4 in the AP poll but just No. 11 in the CFP rankings, with selection committee chairman Hunter Yurachek noting on Tuesday that the Irish did not have a signature win. Not anymore. “This is as good of a win as I’ve ever been a part of and as special of a moment, as special of an outcome that I’ve been a part of since I’ve been the head coach here,” Notre Dame coach Marcus Freeman said during his postgame press conference. That is saying something considering Freeman led the Irish to the national title game in January 2025 after defeating Indiana, Georgia and Penn State in playoff games. But last season, the Irish lost their first two games to Miami and Texas A&M, by far the best opponents on their schedule. The Hurricanes ended up getting the final at-large berth in last year’s CFP because of that victory. And three weeks ago, Notre Dame lost 28-24 at BYU, the only other ranked team besides Miami it will face all season. Kiffin is going through his first season as the Tigers’ head coach following a controversial exit from Ole Miss. item.title: Rob Gronkowski crowns Bill Belichick the ‘GOAT’ with heartfelt tribute at Patriots Hall of Fame ceremony
item.description: Photo by MediaNews Group/Boston Herald via Getty Images Rob Gronkowski has paid a heartfelt tribute to Bill Belichick, calling his former New England Patriots coach the greatest of all time during his Hall of Fame induction ceremony. The former tight end credited Belichick for helping him reach the highest level of the NFL, while also finding room for one of his trademark jokes about his pre-draft meeting. Gronkowski spent nine seasons in New England, winning three Super Bowls alongside Tom Brady and establishing himself as one of the greatest tight ends in franchise history. Rob Gronkowski calls Bill Belichick the greatest coach of all time Speaking during his Patriots Hall of Fame induction, Gronkowski did not hesitate when discussing the coach who helped shape his career. “The greatest of all time, no question about it…Thank you for doing whatever you felt necessary to get me to play at a high level. Thank you for all your hard work and dedication to put our teams in the best possible situations. And thank you for drafting this so-called a**** who would only talk about hot tubs on his pre-draft visits.” The tribute offered a glimpse of the respect Gronkowski still has for Belichick, despite their very different personalities. The former tight end became one of the NFL’s most recognisable players under the famously disciplined coach. Belichick coached New England for 24 seasons and won six Super Bowls with the franchise. Gronkowski was part of three of those championship teams, forming a formidable partnership with Brady. The ceremony also brought several familiar faces from the Patriots dynasty back together. Brady, Julian Edelman, Troy Brown and former offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels were among those in attendance. Brady received a loud ovation from the crowd, with his presence adding to an emotional occasion for the franchise. Gronkowski’s nine seasons in New England produced 521 receptions for 7,861 yards and 80 total touchdowns. He remains the franchise’s all-time leader in touchdowns and ranks second in receiving yards. The former tight end also thanked Patriots supporters for embracing his personality and helping create the famous Gronk persona. Belichick was not in a speaking mood about his former star during the ceremony, but Gronkowski made sure his appreciation was heard. His induction also puts him on course to become eligible for the Pro Football Hall of Fame with the Class of 2027. item.description: Mater Dei players celebrate after beating Sierra Canyon in four sets to win the CIF Southern Section Division 1 championship on Saturday. (Steve Galluzzo / For The Times) Upon hammering her 19th kill on a cross-court attack, Westley Matavao leaped into the arms of her teammates to celebrate Mater Dei’s 24-26, 25-23, 25-21, 25-23 triumph over Sierra Canyon in the CIF Southern Section Division 1 girls’ volleyball final Saturday night at Cerritos College. Having avenged a loss in the section finals last season, the Monarchs’ next goal is to defend their state championship, and they will be the top seed when the Southern California Regional Open Division bracket is released Sunday. Westley Matavao goes on the attack for Mater Dei against Sierra Canyon in the CIF Southern Section Division 1 girls' volleyball championship match on Nov. 7, 2026. (Steve Galluzzo / For The Times) “This season it’s important for us to win everything because I’ve been here all four years, this is my last one and I wasn’t going to take losing as an answer,” said Matavao, a senior outside hitter headed to UCLA. The Monarchs (39-1) have dealt Sierra Canyon (32-2) its only losses this season and the top two programs in the nation could meet for a third time, but for now Mater Dei reigns supreme after earning its second section title in three years. It swept the Trailblazers in the finals two years ago. Freshman Jimin Seung had 14 kills, Cal-bound middle blocker Emma Kingston had 11 kills and sophomore libero Sienna Cicero finished with a match-high 23 digs, diving all over the floor to keep points alive. “It was definitely tougher this time around — over half of them are high Division I level players — so you can’t underestimate a team like that,” Cicero said. “Our blockers played great and funneled the ball perfectly for me. item.title: Why unique Brighton defence is so tricky to unpick
item.description: Fabian Hurzeler got St Pauli promoted to the Bundesliga before leaving for Brighton in June 2024 [Getty Images] "We have a great chance on Saturday to take revenge," were Fabian Hurzeler's words as Brighton exited the Carabao Cup at the hands of Manchester City. The following Saturday, the 33-year-old's dogged defiance manifested in a 1-0 victory over the same opponents, who failed to score at home for the first time in 23 matches. Brighton now sit in third place, only behind City and Premier League leaders Arsenal, both teams they have beaten this season. And they have done so with a bravery and front-footedness that the likes of Arsenal and City have not always been used to facing. With 24 goals in nine games, Brighton are the league's top scorers but it is their defensive work that has underpinned their underdog victories against the league's best teams. Notably, Brighton have conceded just seven goals this season - with only Arsenal conceding fewer. From opposition goal-kicks, Brighton look to press high and in a man-to-man fashion. This is a common approach but Brighton's intensity across the pitch makes them better at executing this than most. The challenge is that the opposition will have an extra player in their build-up compared to Brighton's 10 pressing outfielders, if they use their keeper as a passing option. That potential issue is managed by one of Brighton's attackers leaving the centre-back they began marking - curving their run as they press the opposition keeper. In curving their run, the aim is to cut off the passing angle back to they player they are no longer marking, while the rest of the team are responsible for their direct, individual opponents. In spite of generally opting to play man-to-man across the pitch, at points in their build-up the team in possession may have an unmarked player. This player is usually in an area of the pitch that is hard for them to access - such as their full-back or winger on the far side. This is often an intentional decision Brighton take, believing the benefit of an extra pressing player closer to the ball is greater than the risk associated with leaving that opposing player unmarked. By ensuring the opposing unmarked player is far from the ball, they reduce the likelihood that player is found. By putting more bodies around the ball, they increase the likelihood of winning the ball back. Maxim de Cuyper curves his run as he presses Gianluigi Donnarumma. This makes it hard for City's keeper to pass it to Abdukodir Khusanov. With the angle to City's right side cut off, Brighton also leave Matheus Nunes, the far-side full-back, unmarked, knowing that finding him is difficult. Down City's left, they press man-to-man [BBC] What makes Brighton so unique though is how they defend deeper. Most teams who press high from opposition goal-kicks then settle into a more rigid defensive shape closer to their own goal. Coach Kyle Whittingham ’s odyssey with the Michigan Wolverines looks in serious jeopardy after a bland, borderline embarrassing rivalry game loss to Pat Fitzgerald’s Michigan State Spartans that came after injury concerns dogged MSU’s starting quarterback Alessio Milivojevic . item.description: ANN ARBOR — Not all five-field-goal games are created equally. Five against Toledo, nice. Five against Michigan, better. Much, much better. "Yeah, for sure," fifth-year senior kicker Liam Boyd said with a shy smile following Michigan State's 15-6 win over Michigan at Michigan Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. "This means a ton. Boyd was good from 21, 37, 38, 24 and 49 yards in the victory. Some of them, Fitzgerald could've gone for it on fourth down, but he played the situation game. Michigan State's defense was cooking — Michigan didn't score until there was 1 minute, 35 seconds left — and any points were going to be uber-valuable. "I didn't want to kick any of those," Fitzgerald said afterward, to some laughter. "I told you guys I will be aggressive but not reckless. ... I thought we had the upper hand defensively. ... We were getting stops. "If it was a shootout," Fitzgerald continued, "I'd probably play those plays a little differently." He added, of Boyd, "Full confidence and belief in Liam." item.title: France facing fly half crisis for Springboks clash after Romain Ntamack injury
item.description: France are facing a fly half crisis for their clash with South Africa after losing Romain Ntamack to a shoulder injury. Ntamack was forced off in the first half of the 54-17 win over Fiji in Lyon grasping his left shoulder, with head coach Fabien Galthie confirming afterwards that the issue was “pretty serious” and likely to rule him out of the remainder of the Nations Championship. Galthie is already without Matthieu Jalibert and Thomas Ramos , with Antoine Hastoy another of his playmaking options sidelined. Stade Francais fly half Louis Carbonel, who has five caps, has been summoned to the squad to prepare for the Springboks, while uncapped youngster Axel Desperes has begun the season in good form for Pau. It appears likely, though, that Galthie may pair captain Antoine Dupont and Maxime Lucu in the halves in Paris on Friday. The two scrum halves are each capable at No 10, with Lucu starting there recently for Bordeaux Begles in the Investec Champions Cup against Gloucester. Antoine Dupont could be paired with fellow scrum half Maxime Lucu (Reuters) Veteran centre Gael Fickou has meanwhile been recalled to the France squad as he looks to add to his 98 caps, with wing Teddy Thomas is rewarded for his form for Toulouse more than five years on from his last international appearance. Julien Marchand also bolsters the hooking options having made his Top 14 return on Saturday..

item.title: Bayern Munich star Harry Kane is top footballer, great human per Brad Friedel
item.description: (Photo by Johannes Simon/Getty Images) | Getty Images Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or triumph continues to earn praise from across the football world, and former United States international Brad Friedel is the latest to celebrate the Bayern Munich striker’s achievement. Friedel believes Kane was absolutely deserving of the award, although he acknowledged that Lamine Yamal and Rodri were also worthy candidates. Ultimately, the sheer volume of goals Kane produced made his case difficult to overlook. Friedel also touched on something particularly interesting: winning the Ballon d’Or requires more than simply being an outstanding footballer. It means convincing people across different countries and football cultures that you are the best in the world. “I think that I would have [voted for Kane]. I think that the three best in my mind were him, Lamine (Yamal) and Rodri. I think Lamine and Rodri, especially Rodri in World Cup and what he’s done on both fronts has been remarkable,” Friedel told Gambulls . “But I think for the amount of goals that H scored, it’s truly remarkable. So, I wouldn’t have argued or complained if any of them won, but I’m really happy that Harry won. “Winning a Ballon d’Or, I don’t think you ever think [it was clear Kane would reach this level]. Maybe if you were around Messi or Maradona in the early days, maybe not even Ronaldo. And I was with Michael Owen when he was really young as well. And he won, so you never, you never fully know, they’re going to be that good. “But winning a Ballon d’Or, that’s something different, because you’ve got to want a lot of different nations to think you’re great also. So you never, never know. But as far as a human being? Top, one of the best. Absolutely. One of the greatest strikers of the ball that I’ve been around for sure. And I’m really happy for him, just as a human element that he wanted it.” That final sentiment might be the most meaningful part of Friedel’s assessment. Beyond the goals, records, and individual accolades, he praised Kane’s character and the determination that drove him toward the biggest individual honor in football. Kane has spent years being one of the most prolific strikers in the world, but now he has the Ballon d’Or to show for it.
